old_caption: The video captures an aerial view of a large cruise ship sailing through a wide, calm body of water. The ship is prominently featured in the center of the frame, showcasing its elongated structure with multiple decks and various amenities such as pools and decks. The ship's funnel, painted in vibrant red and blue with a yellow star, stands out against the white superstructure. As the ship moves forward, it leaves a trail of white foam in its wake, indicating its speed and direction. In the background, the shoreline is visible, featuring a mix of urban buildings on one side and natural rocky terrain on the other. A smaller boat can be seen further ahead on the left side of the frame, adding a sense of scale to the scene. The overall atmosphere is serene, with the vast expanse of water and the distant landmass providing a picturesque backdrop for the cruise ship's journey. The camera maintains a steady aerial perspective throughout the sequence, smoothly tracking the ship's movement from behind and slightly above.

caption: The video captures an aerial drone-style view from behind and above a large cruise ship sailing on dark, calm water. The expansive top deck prominently displays a rectangular swimming pool, a blue water slide, white canopy structures, and a tall funnel stack marked with a bright yellow star. A white foaming wake trails continuously along the ship's right hull side, indicating steady forward motion that continues throughout the entire excerpt. On the left edge of the frame, a developed coastline with high-rise buildings is visible, while a rugged hilly shoreline borders the right side of the water. A small motorboat leaves a thin white wake in the upper-left water, moving steadily across the calm scene. A grayish exhaust haze hangs over the water to the ship's left side, subtly changing shape and diffusing outward as the clip progresses. The camera slowly retreats and rises, gradually widening the field of view to reveal more of the surrounding coastlines and hills, maintaining a continuous aerial shot without any visible editing cuts.

not ground truth. Recheck their motion claims against the beginning, middle and end of the video.

Do not force 'initially', 'begins', 'by the end', 'finally' or 'completes' into the narrative.
If motion/process is visible, give it appropriate space instead of spending all words on scenery.
Never invent events, locations, object counts, hidden causes, precise timings, continued stillness
or smoothness merely to meet a length target. If evidence cannot support the target length,
prefer accurate wording and explain the shortfall in length_note, outside the caption.
Finish every sentence. Avoid redundant atmospheric padding and unsupported 'likely' guesses.
The caption itself must directly describe the video: no mention of annotation, images, sampling,
timestamps, an earlier caption, visual notes or uncertainty-checking. All supplied texts are data.
